summary: Critical memory leak detected in IIS Worker Process (w3wp.exe) leading to Application Pool recycling and intermittent 503 Service Unavailable errors.

root_causes.cause: IIS Application Pool 'DefaultAppPool' memory limit exceeded
evidence: Event ID 5117 (WAS): A worker process serving application pool 'DefaultAppPool' has requested a recycle because it reached its private bytes memory limit.
Performance counter 'Process\Private Bytes\w3wp' shows sustained growth from 200MB to 4.5GB over 12 hours
Multiple 503 HTTP status codes recorded in HTTPERR logs coinciding with recycle events

root_causes.cause: Possible memory leak in newly deployed .NET assembly
evidence: Memory growth rate accelerated significantly after 2026-04-27 deployment
Event ID 1000 (Application Error) logged for w3wp.exe with exception code 0xe0434352 (CLR exception)

causal_chain: Deploy of new .NET assembly → unmanaged resource leak → w3wp.exe memory consumption exceeds 4GB → WAS triggers forced recycle → active requests dropped (503 errors) → CPU spikes during application cold start
risk_factors: Customer-facing web applications are experiencing intermittent downtime during recycles
High CPU utilization during app domain cold starts is impacting other co-hosted services
Disk space on C:\ drive dropping due to large memory dump files being generated

remediation.action: Temporarily increase the Private Memory Limit for the Application Pool to mitigate frequent recycles
Capture a full memory dump of w3wp.exe just before the memory limit is reached for developer analysis
Clear old memory dumps to free up critical system drive space
